title: Bald Eagle — motion blurred
subtitle: Two bald eagles in mid-air confrontation. The original RAW is significantly motion-blurred from the eagle's wing motion combined with shutter speed. Tests Topaz Photo's two subject-sharpening modes — Focus Blur vs Motion Blur — for how well each recovers apparent sharpness on the bald eagle's head and wings.
exif_summary: OM-1 with M.150-400mm F4.5 TC + MC-14 at 700mm (1402mm equivalent), 1/3200s at f/8, ISO 800

images.title: RAW
images.caption: RAW images which is very blurred

critique.text: As noted in the caption, this original RAW image is 'very blurred' and suffers from severe technical flaws that significantly detract from its overall quality. Sharpness is exceptionally poor; the entire frame, especially the interacting eagles, is extremely soft, completely lacking any fine detail or distinct edges. This appears to be a result of missed focus, subject motion blur, or a combination of both. Furthermore, there is a prominent, coarse layer of luminance noise visible across the entire image, most noticeably muddying the darker plumage of the birds and the background snow. As a whole, the image is poor in its unedited state because the action of the main subjects is obscured by the lack of clarity. The two Topaz edited versions demonstrate how aggressive AI processing can attempt to salvage such a file by tackling the heavy noise and reconstructing sharp edges, though both introduce artificial textures in the process, with the Motion Blur edit performing slightly better overall.

images.title: Topaz Photo 2
images.caption: Topaz Photo with sharpening on subject using Motion Blur setting at 100

critique.text: This edit, utilizing Topaz Photo's Motion Blur reduction setting at 100, represents a significant rescue effort over the severely blurred original RAW. Noise has been aggressively reduced, resulting in a much cleaner, smoother background. In terms of sharpness, the improvement is dramatic; the subjects, particularly the eagle on the right, now display distinct feather details, a clear eye, and a defined beak that were completely lost in the original. However, pushing the sharpening so heavily has inevitably introduced visible processing artifacts. The textures can appear somewhat 'crunchy' or artificially generated upon close inspection, and the hard edges of the birds feel slightly unnatural against the smoothed snow. Despite these artifacts, this edit is the most successful of the set. It provides the best balance of recovering necessary subject detail while managing the artificial look, making a previously unusable image visually compelling.

images.title: Topaz Photo 1
images.caption: Topaz Photo with sharpening on subject using Focus Blur setting at 100

critique.text: This version applies Topaz Photo's Focus Blur reduction setting at 100 to combat the original's severe softness. Like the first edit, it successfully eliminates the pervasive noise of the RAW file, yielding a clean background, and drastically increases the sharpness of the eagles. However, compared to the Motion Blur edit, the artifacts here are slightly more distracting and less natural. The textures on the feathers feel more brittle and 'painterly,' distinctly showing the heavy hand of AI intervention. The tail feathers of the left eagle, in particular, exhibit somewhat strange, blocky patterns where the software struggled to reconstruct detail. The contrast between the hyper-sharpened subjects and the smooth background makes the eagles look somewhat pasted into the scene. While it achieves the goal of making the subjects sharp, the overall aesthetic suffers slightly more from processing trade-offs than the Motion Blur version.
